audited_conclusions: Ran(E) is a two-sided algebraic radical of the global spectral Weil pairing on the stated codimension-two source class; this does not assume RH.
The source does not prove that a hard-window complement carries a positive Weil leakage form.

Zero-extended finite prolate functions are bounded-variation rather than Schwartz. Extending the Mellin zero-evaluation calculation to them and defining the absolutely convergent bilinear tail bookkeeping is a new lemma, not a quoted theorem; this alone does not extend the source closed Weil form to a global BV vector.
The positive trace cutoff in Connes 1999 cannot be identified with the finite Weil form: the asserted global trace-formula limit is RH-equivalent.
No estimate of the even or odd complementary Weil-sector floor follows from the radical identity.
